w10_P4_000850: A linear test rig in a materials lab drives a small trolley along a rail, and the trolley's speed is given, in metres per second, by 5*t^3 + 3*t^2 with t in seconds. The trolley assembly has a mass of 2000 g. The engineers are interested in the instant t = 1 s, when the drive must supply exactly the force needed to produce the trolley's rate of change of speed. A calibration spring in the coupling adds a constant 26 N on top of that force. The control panel reports the resulting coupling load in kilonewtons. A full production line contains 12 identical rigs pulling together on a shared support frame, and that frame is itself pre-tensioned to 3 kN. What total load, in kN, does the support frame carry?
w10_P4_000851: On a packaging line a shuttle is driven along its rail by 3 identical magnetic stages. Each stage raises the shuttle's speed by 9 m/s while it charges and by a further 7 m/s while it discharges. Once the shuttle leaves the last stage a spring kicker adds another 4 m/s, and the shuttle then travels at that speed. The loaded shuttle has a mass of 59000 g. A latch at the end of the rail holds a further 12 J, which is added to the shuttle's energy of motion to give the figure logged for one shuttle. Each line runs 11 shuttles at once, and the plant operates 9 identical lines. What total energy, in J, does the plant have in play at that moment?
w10_P4_000852: A robotics test bench has 8 fixed anchor points, and any two of them may be joined by a single tension cable. The workshop first counts every distinct pair of anchor points that could be joined in this way. Of those pairs, 19 are ruled out because the machine frame runs between them. Each of the 3 identical test cells in the hall is wired to the same surviving pattern, and across the hall a further 9 cables are held back as spares. The controller then launches the test sled at a speed, in metres per second, numerically equal to the number of cables actually in service. The sled has a mass of 21000 g. What is the sled's energy of motion at launch, in kJ?
w10_P4_000853: A crane maker needs the total pull, in kilonewtons, carried by one bank of gantry hoists. Each hoist drives a carriage whose speed along its beam is, in metres per second, 3*t^3 + 0*t^2 with t in seconds. The carriage assembly has a mass of 168000 g. At the instant t = 1 s the drive supplies exactly the force needed to produce the carriage's rate of change of speed, and a counterweight relieves 10 N of that force. The relieved figure is what the maker records for one hoist, expressed in kilonewtons. A bank contains 8 identical hoists working together. What total pull, in kN, does the bank carry?
w10_P4_000864: A conveyor's high-speed drive is being commissioned. The carriage's rate of change of speed a, in m/s^2, satisfies a^2 - 12a + 32 = 0, and the high-speed setting corresponds to the larger of the two values that fit. The moving carriage has a mass of 138 kg, and the control cabinet beside it is held at 21 degrees C. The drive must supply exactly the force needed to give the carriage that rate of change of speed, and the commissioning sheet records that force in kilonewtons. One bank contains 8 such carriages pulling together, and a counter-tension of 26 kN acts against the bank in the opposite direction. The plant has 3 identical banks. What is the plant's net figure, in kN?
w10_P4_000869: An automation supplier is quoting the total thrust, in newtons, that one of its transfer lines can deliver. Each pusher on the line has a ramp rate r, in m/s^2 per notch, given by the smaller value that satisfies r^2 - 9r + 8 = 0. The controller always runs a pusher at 6 notches, so the moving assembly's actual rate of change of speed is 6 times that ramp rate. The moving assembly of a single pusher has a mass of 173000 g, and each pusher supplies exactly the force that produces this motion. One frame carries 5 pushers, and the line is built from 5 identical frames. What total thrust, in N, does the line deliver?
w10_P4_000873: A forge is totalling the energy, in joules, that its hammer hall has in play. On one rig a 13 kg ram is brought up to speed by 6 identical drive passes, and each pass adds 5 m/s while the ram is loaded and a further 7 m/s while it is released. The ram then strikes at that speed, and its energy of motion is what the log records for a single strike. Each rig makes 5 strikes in a cycle, and a damper bleeds off 18 J from the cycle total. The hall runs 5 cycles in the period being counted, and it contains 3 identical rigs. What is the hall's total figure, in J?
w10_P4_000880: In a lift-testing tower the cage's rate of change of speed a, in m/s^2, is the smaller value satisfying a^2 - 9a + 18 = 0. The cage and its frame together have a mass of 159000 g, and the hoist supplies exactly the force needed to produce that motion. The load cell in the rope is offset, so 14 N must be taken off the hoist's force to obtain the reading. A guide brush then drags off a further 6 N from that reading. Each shaft is fitted with 3 identical cages, and the tower has 9 shafts. What total reading, in N, does the tower log across every cage?
w10_P4_000882: An engine test bench logs the slider's rate of change of speed, in m/s^2, as the area under the curve 5*x^2 + 5*x between x = 3 and x = 4, where x is the crank angle in radians. The slider assembly has a mass of 126 kg, and the bench oil is held at 68 degrees C throughout the run. The drive supplies exactly the force needed to produce that motion, and a friction correction of 21 N is then subtracted from it. One bench carries 6 identical sliders, one hall holds 10 such benches, and the company runs 12 identical halls. What is the company's total corrected drive force, in N?
w10_P4_000883: A logistics depot runs powered carts on a short straight test loop. On the loop a cart's speed v, in m/s, is the smaller value that satisfies v^2 - 12v + 32 = 0. A loaded cart has a mass of 41 kg, and the loop is kept at 18 degrees C for the trial. The cart's energy of motion is measured, and 23 J is deducted from it for the wheel losses. The depot records the deducted figure in kilojoules and multiplies it by the 3 carts it runs together. A charged buffer battery contributes a further 3 kJ to the depot's stored total. What is the depot's stored total, in kJ?
w10_P4_000885: A gear shop is cutting a matched pair of timing belts. One belt has 151 teeth and the other has 33 teeth, and the setter needs the largest whole number of teeth that divides both counts exactly, since that fixes the repeat length of the marking pattern. The test carriage is then run at a speed, in metres per second, numerically equal to that number. The carriage has a mass of 40000 g. Its energy of motion is measured, 4 J is subtracted for the bearing loss, and the corrected figure is multiplied by the 7 identical carriages on the rig. A pre-charged latch then contributes a further 15 J to the rig's total. What is the rig's total figure, in kJ?
w10_P4_000886: A drop-test laboratory needs the net energy figure, in kJ, for its quarterly accounts. The trolley on one rig is brought up to speed by a numbered sequence of pushes: push number k adds k m/s, and the pushes run from k = 1 through k = 5, so the trolley leaves the last push at the accumulated speed. The trolley has a mass of 5 kg, and the hall around it is kept at 19 degrees C. The trolley's energy of motion at that speed is expressed in kilojoules and doubled, because the laboratory owns 2 identical rigs. It is doubled again for the 2 shifts that were run. Finally the chiller's draw of 22 kJ is subtracted from that total. What is the laboratory's net figure, in kJ?
w10_P4_000890: A rail workshop wants the net stored-energy figure, in kilojoules, for its bank of test sleds. Each sled runs at a speed v, in m/s, given by the larger value that satisfies v^2 - 14v + 48 = 0. A single sled has a mass of 37000 g, and its energy of motion at that speed is recorded in kilojoules. A bank holds 8 identical sleds, and the workshop operates 7 such banks. A standing overhead of 3 kJ is then subtracted from the workshop's combined figure. What is the workshop's net figure, in kJ?
w10_P4_000896: A materials laboratory wants the final logged figure, in kilojoules, from its impact bench. The striker's release speed v, in m/s, is the smaller value that satisfies v^2 - 11v + 24 = 0. The striker has a mass of 51000 g, and the bench frame is held at 35 degrees C during the test. The striker's energy of motion at release is expressed in kilojoules, and the bench fires 8 identical strikers in each test. From that combined figure 12 kJ is subtracted to account for the frame's absorption. A pre-charged accumulator then adds 23 kJ to what remains. What is the final logged figure, in kJ?
w10_P4_000900: A press shop is commissioning a new feed drive. The feed carriage's rate of change of speed a, in m/s^2, is the larger value satisfying a^2 - 11a + 24 = 0. The carriage has a mass of 160 kg, and the drive supplies exactly the force required to produce that motion. The commissioning sheet records this force in kilonewtons. The shop runs 5 identical feed drives, and a fixed counterweight of 17 kN pulls against their combined effort. What net figure, in kN, goes on the commissioning sheet?
w10_P4_000901: A quarry contractor needs the final rated pull, in newtons, for a conveyor take-up installation. The base ramp rate r, in m/s^2, is the smaller value satisfying r^2 - 9r + 8 = 0, and the gearing is such that the take-up carriage sees 10 times that rate. The carriage has a mass of 164000 g, and the gearbox oil sits at 45 degrees C. Each drive supplies exactly the force needed to produce the carriage's motion, and the contractor operates 11 identical take-up units. A guide seal absorbs 23 N of the combined pull, and a return spring absorbs a further 25 N. What is the final rated pull, in N?
w10_P4_000903: A CNC shop is checking the drive on a cutting head. The head's speed along the rail is, in metres per second, 3*t^3 - 2*t^2 with t in seconds, and the coolant supply sits at 12 degrees C throughout. The shop is interested in the instant t = 3 s, when the head has a mass of 14 kg and the drive supplies exactly the force needed to produce the head's rate of change of speed at that moment. A magnetic counterbalance takes 13 N off that force. Each machine carries 5 identical heads, and the shop owns 3 identical machines. What total force, in N, do the shop's drives supply?
w10_P4_000906: A hoist manufacturer is testing a winch carriage on the bench. The carriage's rate of change of speed a, in m/s^2, is the larger value satisfying a^2 - 4a + 3 = 0. The carriage has a mass of 103000 g, and the test hall is kept at 24 degrees C. The winch supplies exactly the force needed to produce that motion, a drag chain adds 5 N to the winch's load, and a cable clamp adds a further 12 N. The datasheet quotes this load in kilonewtons. The manufacturer's standard rig runs 5 identical carriages together. What total load, in kN, does the standard rig carry?
w10_P4_000907: A sports-science lab wants the final entry, in kilojoules, on one page of its energy ledger. A treadmill belt's speed follows, in metres per second, 1*t^3 + 2*t^2 with t in seconds, and the technicians differentiate that speed 2 times and read the result at the instant t = 1 s. The control system then launches a test sled at a speed, in metres per second, numerically equal to that result. The sled has a mass of 9000 g, and its energy of motion is written into the ledger in kilojoules. The lab ran 2 identical launches that day. An 8 kJ line for the heater and a 7 kJ line for the lighting are then added to the same page. What is the final entry, in kJ?
w10_P4_000913: A test track logs the energy of a series of sled launches. The sled's launch speed, in metres per second, is the sum of the run numbers k from k = 1 up to k = 8, because each run adds its own number in metres per second to the sled. The sled has a mass of 47000 g, and its energy of motion at launch is what the log records for one launch. The track performs 10 identical launches in a session. A pre-charged latch then contributes 13 J to the session total, and a trigger coil contributes a further 2 J. What total energy, in J, does the session record?
w10_P4_000915: A cable-car workshop needs the total figure, in kilojoules, for the day's test schedule. A car's nominal speed, in metres per second, starts as the sum of the whole numbers from 1 up to 11, one metre per second for each numbered winding stage. From that starting figure 12 is subtracted for drum slip and a further 30 is subtracted for cable stretch, and what remains is the car's actual speed in metres per second. The car has a mass of 42 kg, and its energy of motion at that actual speed is expressed in kilojoules. The workshop tests 12 identical cars during the day. What is the day's total figure, in kJ?
w10_P4_000918: A ballistics laboratory is totalling the energy, in joules, from a morning of rail-launcher shots. In each shot the projectile is accelerated by a train of pulses: pulse number k contributes 2*k - 1 m/s, and the pulses run from k = 1 up to k = 4, so the projectile leaves at the accumulated speed. The projectile has a mass of 40000 g, and its energy of motion at that speed is the base figure for one shot. A sabot spring adds 15 J to each shot's figure. The laboratory fires 7 shots from each magazine and empties 6 magazines during the morning. What is the morning's total, in J?
w10_P4_000919: A shipyard needs the total pull, in kilonewtons, on a winch gantry. The base rate a, in m/s^2, is the smaller value satisfying a^2 - 9a + 18 = 0, and the gearbox multiplies that base rate by 5. A control offset then adds 17 to the geared figure, giving the carriage's actual rate of change of speed in m/s^2. The carriage has a mass of 14000 g, and each winch supplies exactly the force needed to produce that motion. The gantry carries 9 identical winches working together. What total pull, in kN, does the gantry carry?
w10_P4_000932: A skate-park engineer is instrumenting a trolley on a straight run. The trolley's speed v, in m/s, is the larger value that satisfies v^2 - 12v + 32 = 0. The trolley has a mass of 6000 g, and its energy of motion at that speed is measured at the end of the run. A rolling loss of 29 J is then subtracted from the measurement. The run is repeated with 6 identical trolleys, and the engineer wants their combined corrected energy. What is that combined figure, in kJ?
w10_P4_000937: A crane maker wants the total drive force, in newtons, for a whole installed fleet. Each hoist's rate of change of speed, in m/s^2, is the sum of the whole numbers from 1 up to 12, one for each of its numbered gear steps. The hoist drum assembly has a mass of 164 kg, and the machine room is kept at 26 degrees C. Each hoist supplies exactly the force needed to produce that motion, a tower carries 12 identical hoists, and a fixed rigging allowance of 30 N is taken off the tower's combined force. A site has 10 identical towers, and the maker has completed 12 identical sites. What is the fleet's total drive force, in N?
